description: Fixtures for the run-target path layout, generated from the owning implementation. Consumers vendor this file verbatim and assert against it rather than transcribing the tables by hand.

state_root.note: No override and no XDG variable: the built-in default.
The XDG rung, which appends "workbench" to the value.
The override rung, taken verbatim with nothing appended.
The override wins over the XDG rung.
An exported-but-empty override is unset. `export WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR=` in a profile leaves the variable present and empty; reading it as a real override resolves the root to the caller's cwd or to /.
An exported-but-empty XDG variable is unset, per the spec.

slug.note: The ordinary case: already a legal component, unchanged.
Underscores survive; only the separators collapse.
A run of legal dashes is content, not a separator to collapse.
The dot survives. A mirror guessing [^a-z0-9-] gives release-v1-2-3 — a second directory for one target, which is #680 again for every dotted branch.
Leading and trailing dashes are stripped after substitution.
The shape a bot actually produces, with every legal character class in it.

repo_key.note: canonical "acme/widget" — every spelling of one repo takes one key.
A trailing slash hides the .git from a strip that runs before it.
`git clone .../repo/.git` is a spelling git accepts. The strip uncovers a trailing slash, so slashes normalize on both sides of it.
A port is part of the authority, not the path.
Userinfo is part of the authority.
file:// names no host whatever authority it carries: git ignores a file URL's authority and clones the path, so all three of these are one target.
An ~/.ssh/config Host alias. Scp-style with no "user@", which git accepts and which therefore has to be qualified like any other hosted remote.
A hosted remote naming a single segment.
The whole path below the host, not its last two segments — group-a/platform/api and group-b/platform/api are different repos.
A local remote keys on its trailing segment alone — leading directories are machine-specific, so keying on them gives one repo a key per machine.
A remote naming no path names no repo. Keying the userinfo, the host, or a file URL's discarded authority would give every such URL one directory.

The canonical form folds A-Z to a-z and drops one trailing ".git" through that same fold: GitHub and GitLab treat a repo path case-insensitively, so every casing of one path is one repo and takes one lock.

A-Z and nothing else. É (U+00C9) is left as it is, so the mirror never has to agree with this runtime about a Unicode version or a locale. The price is these two rows: a mixed-case non-ASCII path is two keys, not one.
Segments that slug to nothing contribute nothing readable; the digest is what keeps them apart. Without it every such repo under acme/ shares a key.
Nothing readable at all: the key is the digest alone.
A lossy slug, not an empty one. The readable part collides deliberately.
The slug's separator is legal inside a segment, and its strip('-') eats an edge hyphen. Both readable parts collide; both keys do not.
Relative components survive as readable text, never as a path component: the digest suffix means no key can be "." or "..".

target_dir.note: The branch slug never folds case — git refs are case-sensitive, so feat/A and feat/a are two branches and must not share a lock.
